slides.say: a and b are positive integers. Given: a is smaller than b, and a times b, plus four a, is equal to forty-eight. Which of the following cannot be the value of a plus b?

Honestly, it's not obvious where to start here. So let's start with what we can do. We have an equation, and a appears in both terms on the left. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, taking out a common factor, and then plugging in the answers.
[short pause] a is in both terms, so I take it out as a common factor. a times b, plus four a, is a times, in brackets, b plus four. And that's forty-eight.
So now it's a product of two whole numbers that equals forty-eight. Remember breaking a number into pairs. Here we break forty-eight into two factors, and they don't have to be primes.
at: a product of two whole numbers

slides.say: Which factor is a? The smaller one. Why? b is bigger than a, and b plus four is even bigger. So a is the small factor, and b plus four is the big one.
One times forty-eight. a is one, b plus four is forty-eight, so b is forty-four, and a plus b is forty-five.
Two times twenty-four. b plus four is twenty-four, so b is twenty, and a plus b is twenty-two. Not a choice, keep going. Three times sixteen. b is twelve, and a plus b is fifteen.
Four times twelve. b is eight, still bigger than four, and a plus b is twelve.

Five doesn't divide forty-eight. Six times eight? b plus four is eight, so b is four, and that's smaller than six. Not allowed. And after that, the factors swap, and a would be the bigger one. So no more options.
So the sums can be forty-five, twenty-two, fifteen and twelve. Seventeen isn't one of them, so choice number three is our answer.
[pause] Now let's try plugging in the answers. Three choices can be the sum, and one can't. So for each sum, I try small values of a, and b is the sum minus a. Then I check a times b, plus four a.
Forty-five. a is one, so b is forty-four. One times forty-four is forty-four, and four times one is four. Forty-four plus four is forty-eight. It works, out.

Fifteen. a is three, b is twelve. Three times twelve is thirty-six, and four times three is twelve. Thirty-six plus twelve, forty-eight. Out. Twelve. a is four, b is eight. Four times eight is thirty-two, and four times four is sixteen. Thirty-two plus sixteen, forty-eight. Out.

Seventeen. a is one, b is sixteen, sixteen plus four is twenty. a is two, b is fifteen, thirty plus eight is thirty-eight. a is three, b is fourteen, forty-two plus twelve is fifty-four, already above forty-eight. Four and thirteen give fifty-two plus sixteen, sixty-eight, and five and twelve give sixty plus twenty, eighty. It keeps growing, so it never comes back to forty-eight.
So seventeen can't be the sum, choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
